text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bund futures were unchanged in late trade after spending the day shrugging off a steady stream of economic data and comments from top Bundesbank officials. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.59, up 0.18 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - December gilts settled flat on the day on Tuesday despite trading down for most of the day. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-27/32, up 02/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures were saved by a rally in the U.S. bond market after weaker than expected U.S. statistics, which eroded earlier losses and left the contract little changed on the day. The September bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.28 unchanged from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures slid just before the close after a late recovery on a Treasuries rally on talk the EU accounting commission had ruled against French deficit-reduction plans to meet EMU criteria, traders said. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 122.90 down 0.35 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices were sharply higher at midday on Tuesday after getting a two-stage boost -- first from a more moderate-than-expected rise in the third-quarter employment cost index (ECI), and next from a drop in October consumer confidence. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-12/32, up 15/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.71 percent.

JAPAN -The yield of the benchmark 182nd Japanese government bond rose on Tuesday after September industrial output data came in toward the higher end of the market's expectations. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.45, down 0.05 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - LONDON - The primary market passed a quiet session on Tuesday morning with the new issues calendar looking pretty sparse ahead of a holiday in several European centres on Friday when key U.S. jobs data are also due. Activity was confined to retail-targeted offerings headed by the European Investment Bank adding another 250 billion lire to its recent 10-year offering.
